stories.title: Anthropic mathematician claims Riemann hypothesis proof
stories.summary: A mathematician at Anthropic claims to have proved the Riemann hypothesis using the Claude large language model. The hypothesis, first proposed in 1859, remains the most famous unsolved problem in mathematics. The company has not yet provided the peer-reviewed evidence for the claim.

stories.title: OpenAI proposes shared training limits based on perplexity
stories.summary: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki has published the company's internal perplexity metrics, which measure how well a model predicts the next word. He proposed that AI labs agree on shared training limits to monitor model behavior. The company clarified that it is not calling for a pause.

stories.title: Anthropic Mathematician Claims Claude-assisted Riemann Proof - Dataconomy
OpenAI publishes internal pretraining metrics
stories.summary: OpenAI has published internal log-perplexity trends from GPT-3.5 onward to advocate for an industry-wide cap on AI development. The company, which typically treats such data as trade secrets, suggests that labs should agree on development limits and cross them only after establishing better monitoring of AI behavior.

stories.title: OpenAI chief scientist calls for shared AI capability ceiling
stories.summary: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki has proposed that AI developers agree on common limits for model capabilities. The proposal suggests that companies commit to not crossing agreed perplexity thresholds until researchers can better understand and monitor AI behavior. CEO Sam Altman has backed the call for industry standards.

stories.title: OpenAI chief scientist seeks industry limits on AI development, CEO Sam Altman agrees - ThePrint
OpenAI scientist proposes industry AI limits tied to model intelligence metric - Reuters
OpenAI Chief Scientist Urges Industry Limits on AI Development - Bloomberg.com
OpenAI researcher argues for perplexity as progress metric
stories.summary: An OpenAI researcher has argued that tracking the pace of training better compressors is the key to understanding AI progress. The post advocates for establishing perplexity, or cross-entropy loss, as a standard metric for measuring the arc of advances in the field.

stories.title: Google and Watch Duty use AI for wildfire alerts
stories.summary: Google and the nonprofit Watch Duty have launched a tool that uses Gemini to transcribe noisy emergency radio feeds into searchable text. The system, developed during a six-month Google.org Fellowship, allows human reporters to verify incidents and issue alerts to communities faster than before.

stories.title: Perplexity: Gemini 4 Neon Agent Use Grew 15% a Day in 3 Days - FourWeekMBA
Apple Builds Autonomous AI Agent To Take On OpenAI And Anthropic - Dataconomy
Google AI Studio is for developers, not consumers
stories.summary: Google AI Studio allows users to test Gemini models and build apps for free. While the free tier includes newer models like Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the terms of service state the tool is for developers and not for consumer use. Human reviewers may read prompts submitted here.

stories.title: Google adds Gemini 4 Neon to model lineup
stories.summary: Google has launched Gemini 4 Neon, a model designed for complex coding and scientific reasoning. It is available through the Gemini app and Google AI Studio. The paid API version costs $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens for those needing extra judgment.

stories.title: L&T Technology Services Launches SDVault.ai™ to Bring Engineering Intelligence to the Software-Defined Vehicle V-Cycle -
L&T Technology Services launches AI-powered engineering platform
stories.summary: L&T Technology Services has introduced SDVault.ai, a platform combining 250 AI agents with rule-based automation. The company claims the tool allows engineering teams to handle 30% to 40% more workload without increasing staff. It is designed to manage software, testing, and compliance for software-defined vehicles.

stories.title: LTTS claims AI agents reduce ticket triage time
stories.summary: L&T Technology Services has launched SDVault.ai, an AI toolchain for automotive manufacturers. The company reports that early pilots show engineering teams can absorb 40% more workload and reduce ticket triage time from four hours to 10 minutes. The platform focuses on software-defined vehicle development and validation.

stories.title: Google previews Tool Retrieval for Gemini API
stories.summary: Google has introduced a Tool Retrieval feature for the Gemini API to assist AI agents managing large libraries of tools. The feature allows agents to load tool descriptions only when needed, rather than carrying them in every request. Google says this should reduce input token counts and latency.

stories.title: PwC India opens AI experience lab in Gurugram
stories.summary: PwC India has opened a facility in Gurugram featuring over 90 AI solutions for manufacturing, infrastructure, and healthcare. The lab is designed to help businesses test applications, simulate operations, and develop solutions. It includes assets spanning agentic AI, robotics, and physical AI for various operational requirements.

stories.title: Sarvam AI targets inference market with Token Factory
stories.summary: Sarvam AI has launched Token Factory, a commercial platform for accessing AI models. Co-founder Pratyush Kumar described it as one of the first large inference offerings in India, intended to address the country's reliance on imported tokens. The startup uses privately procured GPUs to serve multiple open-weight models.

stories.title: Sarvam faces backlash over hosting Chinese AI models
stories.summary: Sarvam is facing criticism for hosting Chinese AI models on its new Token Factory platform. The company launched the service to provide developers and enterprises with access to various models through its own infrastructure. Some in the Indian AI community have questioned the decision to include Chinese options.

stories.title: Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chennai lead AI investment surge
stories.summary: Indian AI startups raised $1.6 billion in equity funding between January and September 2026, a 96 percent increase over the previous year. While funding has nearly doubled, the capital is concentrated in a few cities, with Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Chennai emerging as the primary beneficiaries.

stories.title: Sarvam defends hosting Chinese models
stories.summary: Sarvam AI co-founder Pratyush Kumar said the startup remains committed to indigenous AI, noting it trained its original 105B model using government-subsidized resources. The company recently released an upgraded version of the model with improved reasoning and language capabilities, while maintaining its Token Factory platform for diverse model access.

stories.title: Sarvam upgrades 105B AI model
stories.summary: Sarvam has released an upgraded version of its 105B AI model, claiming it halves costs and doubles speeds. The startup is currently defending its use of private infrastructure for its Token Factory platform while planning future releases for vision and speech applications.

stories.title: Uttar Pradesh seeks AI platform for state departments
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has invited bids for a common AI platform to link state records through Family ID. The proposed stack includes 12 initial applications, such as tools to monitor social media and analyze police records. A master system integrator will have 12 months to implement the project.

stories.title: Maharashtra announces 2026 AI policy
stories.summary: The Maharashtra Cabinet has approved an AI policy aiming to attract 10 thousand crore rupees in investment and create 150,000 jobs by 2031. The policy proposes a state AI mission to promote research and governance, modeled after the national India AI Mission.

stories.title: Large deals drive India's AI funding growth
stories.summary: Indian AI companies raised $1.6 billion in equity funding through September 2026, a 96 percent increase from the previous year. Despite the surge in total capital, the number of deals has declined, as a handful of large funding rounds account for the majority of the money.

stories.title: UK defense AI startup Agon raises $70 million in Series A funding - Traders Union
Everful raises $48.5 million for retail supply chain AI
stories.summary: Everful has raised $48.5 million in Series A funding to connect retailers with Chinese factories. The startup manages the supply chain from order to delivery and currently ships over five million pieces a month. It claims to be on track to reach $100 million in annualised revenue.

stories.title: Ex-Sequoia Boss Backs UK Defense Startup at $450 Million Value - Bloomberg.com
Unsiloed raises $7.5 million for document parsing
stories.summary: Unsiloed AI has raised $7.5 million in seed funding led by Felicis. The startup is building APIs designed to make documents as computable as databases by enabling software to read, extract, and update information. The company was founded by two IIT Kharagpur graduates.

stories.title: Anthropic founders hold significant stakes following IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic founders, all former OpenAI employees, hold stakes estimated at $20 billion each following the company's November IPO. The company, which produces the Claude chatbot, reached a fully diluted valuation of $1.5 trillion. CEO Dario Amodei previously studied physics and biophysics at Caltech and Princeton.

stories.title: Exclusive | Genesis AI, a Robotics Startup, Raises $500 Million - WSJ
Anthropic IPO valuation trails SpaceX
stories.summary: Anthropic closed its first day of trading with a market capitalization of approximately $1.27 trillion, following a $1.5 trillion fully diluted valuation at its IPO. While the company raised significant cash, it remains behind SpaceX, which debuted with a market capitalization exceeding $2 trillion.

stories.title: Notable Capital bet on Anthropic's Series E
stories.summary: Notable Capital invested roughly 10 percent of its $1 billion-plus fund into Anthropic's Series E round at a $61.5 billion valuation. The firm moved forward despite competition from OpenAI and DeepSeek, citing confidence in Anthropic's future. It was the highest valuation the firm has invested at in 25 years.

stories.title: Physiology education evaluates large language models as knowledge providers
stories.summary: A review in Current Research in Physiology examines how educators can use large language models as knowledge providers or receivers. The analysis explores whether AI should generate text for student evaluation or synthesize student-appraised evidence into prose. The study follows OpenAI releasing its free-to-access large language model.

stories.title: Colgate-Palmolive uses AI to predict consumer product interest
stories.summary: Colgate-Palmolive has developed an AI technique that predicts how consumers might respond to new products by having models roleplay as shoppers. Researchers compared these outputs against thousands of human survey responses. The company is now applying its expertise in toothpaste to the simulation of human purchasing decisions.

stories.title: MIT researchers develop AI-driven analog chip design method
stories.summary: MIT researchers have created a technique to help engineers use AI for designing analog integrated circuits. The method aims to streamline prototyping and discover new schemes to improve energy efficiency in sensors and medical monitors. Designing these circuits is currently a cumbersome manual process due to the possibilities.

stories.title: Anthropic and Claude Riemann Hypothesis proof sparks verification debate
stories.summary: Mathematician Levent Alpöge of Anthropic announced a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis using Claude. He released a Lean 4 codebase containing 17 million lines of code rather than a human-readable paper. The verification status remains disputed between those citing vacuous truths and the Lean community.

Independent groups verify Claude-assisted Riemann Hypothesis proof
stories.summary: Two independent groups claim to have verified a Claude-assisted proof of the 170-year-old Riemann Hypothesis. A Fields Medal winner called the breakthrough a historic milestone if it holds. The proof follows OpenAI releasing over 300 mathematical proofs, suggesting a future where AI handles the heavy lifting of mathematics.

Meta releases TLX compiler extension for Triton
stories.summary: Meta has published a report on TLX, a Triton extension that exposes warp groups and barriers to Python kernels. It targets NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell plus AMD MI300 and MI350-series GPUs. The company claims kernel engineers can now achieve CUDA-level control without leaving the Triton environment.

stories.title: Treasury Secretary Bessent demands answers on Nvidia export controls
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is investigating Nvidia over potential export control violations regarding advanced chips sent to China. The investigation includes the company's management and a Singapore-based data center. Bessent stated on November 22 that the administration still requires answers about who supervised the export compliance practices.

stories.title: Alibaba says proprietary chips offset US export restrictions
stories.summary: Alibaba announced its Zhenwu V900 AI accelerator chip will enter mass production early next year. The company claims increasing reliance on its own processors is offsetting US export restrictions on advanced semiconductors. Alibaba continues to use Nvidia chips in data centers outside of China.

stories.title: US Approved Nearly 900,000 AI Chip Sales To China - Dataconomy
L&T secures large order for NVIDIA B300 GPU deployment
stories.summary: Larsen and Toubro has secured a large multi-year order to deploy NVIDIA B300 GPUs at its Chennai data center. The subsidiary LTN Compute will support an inference provider's AI-native platform. The company classifies the contract as large, though it has not disclosed the exact financial value.

stories.title: L&T secures AI infrastructure order for NVIDIA B300 GPUs
stories.summary: Larsen and Toubro has secured a large multi-year order for AI infrastructure deployment. The company, which operates in sectors ranging from defense to hydrocarbon, is trading at a P/E of 30.5. The contract involves the deployment of NVIDIA B300 GPUs to support growing AI computing demand.

stories.title: Treasury Secretary Bessent questions Nvidia export compliance
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that export-control compliance at Nvidia typically falls to the general counsel's office. Bessent confirmed the Treasury lacks answers regarding potential violations involving China. A 10-day window for the board to provide clarity expires around November 25. The answers remain unknown.

stories.title: Nvidia faces deepening pressure over China chip sales
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is demanding clarity on Nvidia's export compliance and whether restricted technology reached China. The investigation into the company's management and sales practices could lead to regulatory penalties. The administration is seeking to identify who was responsible for overseeing the company's export compliance practices.

stories.title: YTL denies report of providing China access to Nvidia chips
stories.summary: Malaysia's YTL Power International denied a media report claiming its data center unit provided Chinese customers with access to Nvidia chips. The company has collaborated with Nvidia since 2023 to build a facility powered by GB 200 GPUs. The data center went live in October 2025.

stories.title: Deloitte India report links AI to cyber insurance shifts
stories.summary: A Deloitte India report notes a 1,200 percent surge in automated phishing, pushing the cyber insurance market toward intelligence-led underwriting. Traditional risk assessment methods are struggling to keep pace with AI-driven threats. Insurers are now expected to rely on real-time behavioral indicators to determine appropriate pricing.

stories.title: Pluxee study finds three paradoxes in employee engagement
stories.summary: Pluxee surveyed 11,000 employees across 14 countries for its latest engagement study. The report claims work plays a smaller role in lives even as company connection grows, and notes employees are ready to quit despite financial pressure. The study offers a vivid snapshot of the current workplace.

stories.title: Tech workers in India eye career changes
stories.summary: A survey of 2,958 technology professionals in India found 72 percent would switch careers if possible. With layoffs and artificial intelligence concerns reshaping the industry, 56 percent of respondents would not encourage their children to enter the field. Only 4 percent would recommend software engineering to new entrants.

stories.title: OpenAI voice models deployed at 1,500 industrial sites
stories.summary: South Korean startup HiLocal has integrated OpenAI APIs into its industrial safety tool, hiWorker. The solution has been deployed at 1,500 construction and manufacturing sites this year, with roughly 100 companies signing supply contracts. OpenAI Korea recently hosted a session on enterprise use cases for voice AI.

stories.title: India pushes for industry-specific AI integration
stories.summary: While India’s AI Mission supports adoption, many enterprises struggle to move beyond isolated pilots. Experts suggest that connecting workflows through industry-specific cloud platforms is more effective than deploying generic tools or replacing legacy ERP systems. The goal is to build a unified data foundation for core operations.

stories.title: Pine Labs releases research on agentic commerce
stories.summary: Pine Labs has launched a research series titled The Agentic Fine Print, authored by INSEAD professor Ben Charoenwong. The project explores the infrastructure and governance required as AI agents begin executing consumer purchases. It invites regulators and payment networks to collaborate on standards for autonomous commerce at scale.

stories.title: AI shifts PR toward data-led communication
stories.summary: Artificial intelligence is being used in India's public relations sector for media observation and content generation. While the industry moves toward data-driven insights and real-time audience prediction, practitioners maintain that human discernment remains necessary to uphold credibility. Tools like VartaLab are currently being used to gauge reactions.

stories.title: Anthropic launches manufacturing-focused AI tool
stories.summary: Anthropic has introduced Claude for Manufacturing, a software offering designed to automate administrative and engineering tasks. The system connects with platforms like Oracle NetSuite and Autodesk Fusion to manage supplier relationships and equipment diagnostics. The company claims the tool is intended to reduce time spent on everyday tasks.

stories.title: Cybersecurity budgets face 2027 adjustments
stories.summary: Businesses are re-evaluating cybersecurity budgets as reliance on single technology providers creates systemic risks. Following global outages and security flaws in widely used software, companies are reconsidering their dependence on individual vendors. The trend suggests a shift toward more comprehensive backup plans for critical business operations.

stories.title: Court denies Blink Digital plea against Meta
stories.summary: The Bombay High Court has refused to restore four disabled Meta Business Manager accounts belonging to Blink Digital. The court held that Meta is not a government agency and does not owe a public duty to permit advertising business. The plaintiff failed to establish a case for intervention.

stories.title: Former OpenAI board member dismisses AI kill switch
stories.summary: Helen Toner, former OpenAI board member, stated that an emergency shutdown mechanism would not resolve rising cybersecurity risks. As US lawmakers consider federal AI regulations, Toner noted that no single kill switch can address the challenges posed by the technology. Shutdown systems may only offer limited protection.

stories.title: California sues OpenAI over safety concerns
stories.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging the company prioritized growth over public safety. The filing claims OpenAI developed products without sufficient oversight and ignored warning signs regarding system security. The state initiated the legal action on November 16.

stories.title: China intelligence agency prioritizes chip acquisition
stories.summary: A New York Times report claims China’s Ministry of State Security has launched a campaign to acquire advanced semiconductor chips. The effort, led by a working group under Chen Yixin, reportedly includes smuggling operations and intelligence gathering on global supply chains to bypass Western export restrictions.

stories.title: Nvidia scandal linked to Chinese intelligence
stories.summary: Sources told ABC News that a woman involved in an alleged affair with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang maintained contact with a Chinese Ministry of State Security official. The communication reportedly occurred between Spring 2025 and Fall 2026, overlapping with her relationship with the former executive.

stories.title: California attorney general sues OpenAI over safety concerns - Investing.com
OpenAI notes emerging AI capabilities
stories.summary: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki says advanced models may develop skills without explicit training. By improving systems to predict information across large datasets, models can demonstrate reasoning and cybersecurity capabilities not directly taught by developers. The findings raise questions about future safety risks as models become more effective.

stories.title: U.S. Tracked Alice Huang’s Contacts With China Spy Agency During Nvidia Affair - The New York Times
Governors seek role in AI regulation
stories.summary: The National Governors Association has unveiled principles to ensure states participate in a shared national approach to AI regulation. Maryland Governor Wes Moore stated that governors aim to protect workers and consumers while maintaining human control. The group plans to engage with the incoming Congress in January.

research.title: A Sparsity Analysis of Traffic Forecasting Architectures: How Much Missing Data is Too Much?
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Traffic forecasting models are typically evaluated under ideal conditions with complete data. This evaluation does not reflect the frequent sensor failures and communication outages common in real-world deployments. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of multivariate. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Action-Conditioned Spatio-Temporal Forecasting
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We study spatio-temporal forecasting in networked systems under specified actions. The challenge is to capture the action's effects without predicting spurious changes in unaffected regions. However, direct supervision and evaluation of these effects require paired futures. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Affine-Image Propagation for Tight and Scalable Neural Network Verification
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: While bound propagation methods are highly effective for certifying neural networks against $\ell_{\infty}$ adversaries, tight and scalable verification for $\ell_{2}$ adversaries remains a significant open challenge. Existing methods incur geometric loss by enclosing preactivation sets in. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: CENTRY: A Probabilistic Latent-State Model for Continual AI Risk Estimation, Monitoring, and Regulation
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, yet existing AI safety frameworks primarily define, categorize, or govern AI risk rather than proposing implementable models and methods for continually estimating, monitoring, and regulating risk. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Coherence by Construction: Synthesizing CTI Knowledge Graphs and the Formal Limits of Coherence Validation
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthesizing relational training data such as knowledge graphs with a large language model typically emits structured objects one at a time, which keeps each object valid but leaves the relationships between them ungrounded. We study an. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Cross-Attack Robust Aggregation for Federated Learning
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning (FL) lets resource-constrained IoT and edge devices train a shared model without exchanging raw data, but compromised or faulty devices can poison the global model. Existing robust aggregators each fail in some regime: naive. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Cross-Linguistic Distinctive-Feature Constraints on Segmental Triphones: Evidence for Contrastive Dispersion
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Natural speech reflects articulatory and perceptual constraints, yet how these pressures shape consecutive segment transitions across languages remains underexplored. We analyze adjacent distinctive-feature distances in token-weighted segmental triphones across 17 Universal Dependencies corpora spanning nine language. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Cross-Platform Production Signatures of State-Linked Information Operations
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: An information operation active on several platforms presents different names, personas, and topics on each. Its working routine is harder to change. We call this routine the operation's production signature: the regularities in when and how. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
